title: Straßenbahn-Neubaustrecke „Neues Uniklinikum Würzburg“ - Geotechnische Baubegleitung
description: Die Würzburger Straßenbahn GmbH (WSB) betreibt im eigenen Namen, auf eigene Rechnung und auf eigenes Risiko auf Grundlage eines öffentlichen Dienstleistungsauftrages gemäß Art. 3 Abs. 1 VO 1370/2007 zwischen der Stadt Würzburg und der WSB im örtlichen Zuständigkeitsbereich der Stadt Würzburg den öffentlichen Personennahverkehr mit Straßenbahnen und Omnibussen. In diesem Gesamtkontext ist die WSB aufgefordert, folgende Linienerweiterung (Gesamtmaßnahme) baulich umzusetzen: Das bestehende meterspurige Straßenbahnliniennetz in Würzburg wird durch die WSB mit der geplanten Baumaßnahme Straßenbahn-Neubaustrecke „Neues Uniklinikum Würzburg“ erweitert. Hierdurch wird das Nordgelände und die geplante Erweiterung des Universitätsklinikums Würzburg (Kopfklinikum, Frauenklinik, Zentrum Operative Fächer ZOM, Zentrum für Innere Medizin ZIM) (UKW) von der Straßenbahn erschlossen und an die Innenstadt von Würzburg angebunden. Für die Durchführung der Gesamtmaßnahme Straßenbahn-Neubaustrecke „Neues Uniklinikum Würzburg“ sind diverse Leistungen für die geotechnische Baubegleitung zu erbringen. Hierzu zählen u.a.: - Probenahmen; - Untersuchungen; sowie - Einbau/Verdichtungskontrolle.

description: Die Würzburger Straßenbahn GmbH (WSB) betreibt im eigenen Namen, auf eigene Rechnung und auf eigenes Risiko auf Grundlage eines öffentlichen Dienstleistungsauftrages gemäß Art. 3 Abs. 1 VO 1370/2007 zwischen der Stadt Würzburg und der WSB im örtlichen Zuständigkeitsbereich der Stadt Würzburg den öffentlichen Personennahverkehr mit Straßenbahnen und Omnibussen. In diesem Gesamtkontext ist die WSB aufgefordert, folgende Linienerweiterung (Gesamtmaßnahme) baulich umzusetzen: Das bestehende meterspurige Straßenbahnliniennetz in Würzburg wird durch die WSB mit der geplanten Baumaßnahme Straßenbahn-Neubaustrecke „Neues Uniklinikum Würzburg“ erweitert. Hierdurch wird das Nordgelände und die geplante Erweiterung des Universitätsklinikums Würzburg (Kopfklinikum, Frauenklinik, Zentrum Operative Fächer ZOM, Zentrum für Innere Medizin ZIM) (UKW) von der Straßenbahn erschlossen und an die Innenstadt von Würzburg angebunden. Für die Durchführung der Gesamtmaßnahme Straßenbahn-Neubaustrecke „Neues Uniklinikum Würzburg“ sind diverse Leistungen für die ökologische Baubegleitung zu erbringen. Hierzu zählen u.a.: - Festlegung und Kennzeichnung der während der Baumaßnahmen zu schützenden Bäume und Sträucher mit Schutzmaßnahmen vor Beginn der Hauptbaumaßnahme (05/2027); - Kontrolle Bäume und Sträucher vor Rodung; sowie - Ökologische Baubegleitung während der gesamten Bauzeit (ca. 5,5 Jahre, Baubeginn 11/2026).

title: Joogiveehaarde seire kohandamise uuring lähtuvalt joogiveehaarde valgala/toiteala riskihindamise tulemustest ja varasematest seireandmete tulemustest (Terviseamet)
description: Projekti eesmärk on töötada välja teaduspõhised ettepanekud ja metoodilised juhised joogivee kvaliteedinäitajate hindamiseks ning seire kavandamiseks joogiveehaarde tasandil. Projekti käigus koostatakse ettepanekud joogivee ohutuse seisukohalt asjakohaste piirsisalduste määramiseks näitajatele, millel need puuduvad ja soovituslikeks seiresagedusteks, töötatakse välja põhimõtted naaberveehaarete varasemate seireandmete kasutamiseks joogiveehaarete riskihindamisel ning kriteeriumid näitajate seiresse võtmiseks olukordades, kus riskihindamise tulemused viitavad võimalikule ohule. Projekti tulemused annavad metoodilise sisendi joogiveehaarete valgala või toiteala riskihindamise läbiviimiseks ja joogiveehaarde vee seire koostamiseks toetades veeseaduse §-st 85 prim 2 tulenevate nõuete rakendamist. Samuti aitab projekt tagada, et joogivee kvaliteedi hindamine põhineks andmepõhistel ja teaduslikult põhjendatud otsustel. / Kõrvaldamise alused ja kvalifitseerimistingimused: Vaata hanke alusdokumentidest

title: Germany – Test boring work – i2030-Nahverkehrstangente Nord, Berlin - Baugrunderkundung
description: Im Rahmen des Infrastrukturprojekts „i2030 – Mehr Schiene für Berlin und Brandenburg“ beinhaltet eine Teilmaßnahme zur Erweiterung und Engpassbeseitigung u.a. die Verlängerung der S-Bahnstrecke von Wartenberg durch das Karower Kreuz und weiter Richtung Schönfließ. Mit dem Neubau der sogenannten Nahverkehrstangente und der Errichtung zusätzlicher Zugangsstellen sollen die nördlichen Stadt- und Entwicklungsgebiete an das S-Bahnnetz angeschlossen werden. Dazu ist u.a. auch die Errichtung eines Turmbahnhofes am Karower Kreuz vorgesehen, um eine Umstiegsmöglichkeit von Ost-West- in Nord-Süd-Richtung und umgekehrt zu ermöglichen. Für diese Maßnahmen sind die Untersuchung und die Beurteilung des Baugrundes erforderlich. Gegenstand der Vergabe sind die dafür erforderlichen Baugrunderkundungen inkl. Feld- und Laborversuche.

title: Romania – Road construction works – Execuție lucrări privind obiectivul de investiție ”Modernizare DJ 595 D Moșnița Veche-Giroc”
description: Prezenta achiziție tratează lucrările de modernizare a drumului județean DJ 595D existent, care își desfășoară traseul în intravilan și extravilan, pe o lungime de 12.090 m (12,09 km) și asigură legătura între localitățile Moșnița Veche și Giroc, respectiv o nouă conexiune cu Varianta Ocolitoare Timișoara (VTM). Durata de execuție a lucrărilor este de 36 luni de la data emiterii ordinului de începere a lucrărilor de către beneficiar, conform documentației de atribuire. Lucrările de modernizare cuprind următoarele tipuri: A. Lucrări de drumuri - modernizarea drumului județean cu o bandă de circulație pe sens; - amenajarea a 10 sensuri giratorii - piste pentru biciclete - trotuare - intersecții cu drumurile și străzile laterale; - accese la proprietăți; - stații de autobuz; - parcări; - realizarea dispozitivelor de colectare și scurgere a apelor pluviale; - realizarea podețelor; - elemente de siguranța circulației; B. Lucrări de căi ferate Lucrările necesare pentru modernizarea trecerii la nivel cu calea ferată CF 125 Timișoara - Buziaș, de la km 9+701.10: - montarea dalelor elastice la capetele dalelor elastice aferente TN modernizate; - racordarea dalelor exterioare TN cu trotuarul modernizat; - amplasarea parapetelor la limita dintre partea carosabilă și trotuare; - amplasarea instalației de semnalizare a apropierii trenurilor fără semibariere de tip SAT; - relocarea stâlpului TTR din zona km 8+607 pe care este montat traseul FO C. Lucrări de instalații electrice - iluminarea intersecțiilor de tip girație D. Lucrări de transport gaze naturale - înlocuirea rețelei de distribuție a gazelor naturale și a branșamentelor conectate la aceste rețele, ce alimentează imobilele existente pe sectorul de drum județean DJ 595D proiectat - protejarea conductelor de transport gaze naturale DN 200 Foieni - Timișoara I și DN 400 Timișoara I - Timișoara III, conform proiectului “Protejare conducte de transport gaze naturale existente DN 200 Foieni - Timișoara I și DN 400 Timișoara I - Timișoara III, la intersecția cu DJ 595D, Moșnița Veche - Giroc, jud. Timiș” E. Lucrări de telecomunicații - realizarea unei infrastructuri subterane formată din tuburi HDPE/PVC și cămine de comunicații pentru punerea în siguranță a rețelelor de telecomunicații subterane și aeriene și asigurarea conexiunii la rețeaua de comunicații a viitorilor abonați. Lucrările vor fi executate în conformitate cu prevederile Proiectului tehnic elaborat de către firma de proiectare – SC Iriconstruct SRL, și a Autorizației de Construire nr. 7 din 26.05.2026 eliberată de Consiliul Județean Timiș. Autoritatea contractantă va răspunde în mod clar și complet tuturor solicitărilor de clarificare /informații suplimentare, în a 12-a zi înainte de termenul limită stabilit pentru depunerea ofertelor, în condițiile în care solicitările se vor adresa cu cel puțin 22 zile înainte de termenul limită stabilit pentru depunerea ofertelor. Clarificările depuse după acest termen nu vor mai fi luate în considerare. Valoarea totală estimată a contractului de execuție lucrări - este de 119.041.724,00 lei, excl. TVA, mediului și nu conține valoarea ”cheltuielilor diverse și neprevăzute” (estimată la 10% din valoarea totală ).

title: Rygge Munitions Storage rea Expansion
description: The purpose of this amendment is to extend the deadline for submission of proposals to 06 October 2026 and to provide updated site drawings and specifications in response toRFIs received......................................................................................................................PROJECT TITLE: RYGGE MUNITIONS STORAGE AREA EXPANSIONPROJECT LOCATION: RYGGE, NORWAYTHIS CONSTRUCTION PROJECT WILL BE A COMPETITIVE, FIRM-FIXED PRICE DESIGN-BID-BUILD CONTRACT PROCURED VIA A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) IN ACCORDANCE WITH FAR PARTS 15 AND 36 AND THE TRADEOFF SOURCE SELECTION PROCESS. THIS IS AN UNRESTRICTED (FULL-AND-OPEN COMPETITION) RFP WITH A BRAND-NAME REQUIREMENT UNDER NAICS CODE 236220. THE SMALL BUSINESS SIZE STANDARD FOR THIS NAICS CODE IS $45,000,000.00.The United States Corps of Engineers Europe District has a requirement on behalf of the United States Air Force (USAF) to build and extend the munitions storage area (MSA) on Rygge Air Station in support of USAF contingency operations in Norway. The project includes the construction of 20 ammunition storage magazines (earth-covered magazines, or ECMs) to accommodate a total Net Explosive Weight (NEW) of 3,000,000 pounds. A standard ammunition storage magazine design which supports up to a maximum capacity of 165,000 pounds NEW will be used for all 20 magazine/bunkers. Supporting facilities include one concrete munitions assembly pad, one stuff on-off pad, gravel roads, bermed areas, lighting, security fencing surmounted by barbed wire, and utility connections for communications and electrical. This project is in direct support of the European Deterrence Initiative (EDI) and the Supplementary Defense Cooperation Agreement (SDCA) between the United States and the Government of Norway, and is intended to be compatible with applicable NATO, DoD, Air Force, and host-nation design standards.

title: Germany – Construction work – Neubau Kita Kruft
description: Bei dem Bauvorhaben handelt es sich um den Neubau einer Kindertagesstätte in der Vulkanstraße in 56642 Kruft. Das Baugrundstück liegt in einem Hanggelände im Nord-Osten der bebauten Ortslage von Kruft. Zufahrt und Andienung der Baustelle erfolgen über die Vulkanstraße als öffentlicher Verkehrsweg. Die Kita wird als T-förmiges Gebäude mit einer Kantenlänge von ca. 42 x 40 m errichtet. Durch die Hanglage wird der Baukörper in der Höhe zweigeschossig gestaffelt: auf Eingangsniveau, das von der Vulkanstraße aus erschlossen wird, befindet sich der Zugang zur Kita, der Verwaltungsbereich, der Mehrzweckraum, das Bistro und die Küche, Technikräume sowie die Krippengruppe mit Nebenräumen. Im "Obergeschoß", das sich ebenerdig zu den Freiflächen am Hang öffnet, befinden sich weitere fünf Gruppenräume mit Neben- und Schlafräumen sowie der Personalräume . Vor den Gruppenräumen befindet sich ein überdachtes Spieldeck, das den Zugang zu dem Außenspielgelände ermöglicht. Das Dach des Baukörpers im Erdgeschoß und Teile des Dachs des Obergeschosses werden extensiv begrünt. Auf der Pultdachfläche des Obergeschosses werden zusätzlich Photovoltaik-Module errichtet. Fläche des Baugrundstückes: insgesamt ca. 13.370 m2 Überbauter Bereich: insgesamt ca. 2.290 m2 Bauteile und Baustoffe: Stahlbetonbodenplatte gemäß Statik und Bodengutachten; Einzelfundamente/Streifenfundamente aus Stahlbeton, nach DIN EN 1992 auf Gründungspolster (Schotter); oberseitige Schweißbahnabdichtung. Außenwände: einschaliges Mauerwerk, d= 36,5cm, aus Wärmedämm-Leichtbetonstein; wärmegedämmte Betonbauteile (Stürze, Stützen, etc.) mit Putz und Anstrich Innenwände: alle tragenden und nichttragenden Innenwände werden in Mauerwerk bzw. in Stahlbeton gem. Statik ausgeführt. Dachkonstruktion EG : Flachdach als massive Stahlbetondecke Dachkonstruktion OG: flach geneigtes Dach in Holzbauweise mit statischen Sonderelementen in Profilstahl; Gefälle ca. 3,5% Dacheindeckung : Warmdach mit Wärmedämmung als Auf- und in Teilen auch Zwischensparrendämmung gem. GEG-Berechnung/-planung, Abdichtung 2-lagig mittels gründachgeeigneter Bitumenschweißbahnen Fensterkonstruktion: Fenster- u. Fenstertüren aus Kunststoff mit 3-fach Isolierverglasung, gem. GEG-Nachweis; Außenfensterbänke aus Aluminium. Große Fenster- und Fenstertürelemente:Aluminium mit 3-fach Isolierverglasung, gem. GEG-Nachweis. Verdunklung/Sonnenschutz: elektr. betriebene Textilscreens und Raffstore je nach Einsatzgebiet. Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung ist das Los 10 Raumlufttechnik.

title: Finland – Electricity – Sähköenergian hankinta
description: Hankinnan kohteena on sähköenergian ja salkunhoitopalvelujen hankinta. Hankinta toteutetaan Sansian hallinnoimana yhteishankintana, jossa tilaajina ovat Mikkelin kaupunki, Etelä-Savon Koulutus Oy, Metsäsairila Oy, Mikalo Oy ja Mikkelin Asumisoikeus Oy. Hankinnassa sähköenergian hinta muodostuu fyysisen sähkön spot-toimituksesta, hintariskin vähentämiseksi tehtyjen tehopohjaisten hinnankiinnitysten selvityksestä, uusiutuvan sähkön alkuperätodistusten hankinnasta, toimittajan marginaalista sekä kantaverkkoyhtiö Fingridin kulloinkin voimassa olevasta tuotannon ja kulutuksen volyymimaksusta. Hankinnan määräaikainen sopimuskausi on 1.1.2029 - 31.12.2030. Sen lisäksi hankintaan sisältyy sopimusosapuolten yhteisesti päätettävä jatko-optio 1.1.2031 -31.12.2032. Tilaajien yhteenlaskettu sähköenergian hankinta on noin 38,2 GWh/vuosi. Ilmoitettu määrä on arvio, jossa esiintyy vuosittaista vaihtelua. Tilaajakohtaisia käyttöpaikkamääriä ja arvioituja sähköenergian hankintamääriä on tarkemmin kuvattu tarjouspyynnön liitteessä. Kaikki esitetyt käyttöpaikkamäärät ja volyymit ovat arvioita, eivätkä hankintayksikkö ja tilaajat sitoudu niiden mukaisiin hankintamääriin. Tarjoajia pyydetään tutustumaan kaikkiin tarjouspyynnön liitteenä oleviin asiakirjoihin ja huomioimaan ne tarjousta tehdessään. Hankintaan valitaan yksi (1) toimittaja.

title: Finland – System maintenance services – Turvajärjestelmien huolto- ja ylläpitopalveluiden hankinta
description: Hankinnan kohteena on Oulun yliopiston ja Oulun Ammattikorkeakoulu Oy:n (OAMK) turvajärjestelmien ylläpitopalvelu. Hankinnan tavoitteena on muodostaa Tilaajalle yhtenäinen toimintamalli turvajärjestelmien ylläpitoon, huoltoon, muutostöihin ja elinkaaren hallintaan. Hankinta koskee Tilaajan turvajärjestelmiä kaikissa sen kohteissa. Hankinnan piiriin kuuluvat myös sopimuskauden aikana käyttöönotettavat uudet kohteet sekä olemassa oleviin kohteisiin toteutettavat laajennukset ja muutokset. Tällä hetkellä Oulun yliopisto toimii ensisijaisena tilaajana ja läpilaskuttaa kustannukset Oulun Ammattikorkeakoululta (OAMK). Sopimuskauden aikana myös Oamkilla voi syntyä omia hankintatarpeita, jotka liittyvät esimerkiksi järjestelmien uudistamiseen tai korvaamiseen. Oulun yliopiston konsulttina tässä kilpailutuksessa toimii Seclion Oy. Hankinnan kuvaus tarkemmin liitteissä "Hankinnan yleiskuvaus" ja "Palvelukuvaus".

Lisäksi hankintayksikkö varaa mahdollisuuden kahteen optiovuoteen 2029 ja 2030. Optiolla tarkoitetaan mahdollisuutta sopimuksen jatkamiseen alkuperäisin ehdoin. Optioiden käytöstä ja kestosta päätetään erikseen. Hankinta tullaan toteuttamaan puitejärjestelynä tarjouspyynnössä kuvatulla tavalla. Hankinnan kohteena ovat elintarvikkeet, päivittäistavarat ja kulutustavarat. Hankinta sisältää mm. seuraavat tuoteryhmät: elintarvikkeet, päivittäistavarat, sisustustuotteet ja kausitarvikkeet, kotikeittiötarvikkeet, muovi- ja säilytystarvikkeet, kertakäyttöastiat, pienelektroniikka ja pienkodinkoneet sekä muut mahdolliset tuoteryhmät, joita ei pystytä erikseen yksilöimään. Hankinta koskee koko Salon kaupunkia ja ostoja tekevät kaupungin eri palvelualueet paikan päällä toimittajan päivittäistavarakaupassa tai myymälässä. Hankinta on jaettu kahteen osa-alueeseen ja tarjoaja voi jättää tarjouksen joko yhteen tai useampaan osa-alueeseen.

title: SPS-02372 Conservation Strategy for Selected SPS Historic Estate Assets
description: The Scottish Prison Service (SPS) requires a suitably qualified multidisciplinary supplier to prepare three (3) Conservation Strategies for selected historic assets across its estate. The commission will cover the following sites: HMP Barlinnie (Glasgow), HMP Castle Huntly (near Dundee) and HMP Perth (Perth). The Conservation Strategies will act as practical, significance-led management tools to support maintenance, repair, operation, adaptation, and future decision-making for historic and listed buildings. The work will include (but is not limited to): 1) Review of baseline information and historic development 2) Building and fabric surveys 3) Structural appraisal input 4) Significance assessments 5) Condition surveys and defect registers 6) Preparation of marked-up drawings showing significance and risk 7) Development of prioritised action plans (short to long term) 8) Maintenance and operational guidance for estates teams 9) Advice on statutory consent and engagement with Historic Environment Scotland and planning authorities 10) Site-specific conservation policies The outputs will comprise three Conservation Strategies, one per site, supported by drawings, action plans, and guidance documents.

This notice DOES NOT constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), Invitation for Bid (IFB), solicitation, or package requesting technical competencies/qualifications of the prospective contractor, nor does it represent any commitment by the Government. Since this is a Sources Sought Notice, no evaluation letters and/or results will be issued to the respondents. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this notice nor does this obligate the Government to award a contract. No telephone calls will be accepted requesting a bid package or solicitation. A solicitation does not presently exist. The Air Force will not accept or acknowledge: emails over 10MB, brochures, samples, catalogs, and any other marketing solicitation information. The Government is performing market research primarily in order to determine if there are firms that possess the capability to execute the requirements of this sources sought notice. Therefore, we further invite all business concerns to provide a capability statement in response to this requirement. Prospective contractors shall be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) prior to award of any Federal Government contract. Contractors are encouraged to obtain further information on SAM registration at the following website: https://www.sam.gov/ If your firm would be interested in such work, you are strongly encouraged to submit a capability statement that addresses as a minimum the questions presented within this notice and submit it to the point of contact listed below by the due date. The Government does not intend to rank submittals or provide any reply to interested firms. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 611430 � Professional and Management Development Training, is applicable to this acquisition. The small business size standard for this NAICS is $15.0M. Following submissions of a capability package, the United States Air Force (USAF) representatives may choose to engage in additional communications with selected respondents only intended to support market research for further clarification of industry capability to meet requirements. The USAF has a requirement in support of the Air Force Civil Engineer Center (AFCEC) to procure a web-based professional development training program providing 3,500 total training hours for the Air Force Total Force (Active Duty, Civilian, Guard, and Reserve). The contractor-provided library must contain more than 2,000 accredited professional/technical engineering and architectural courses yielding Continuing Education Units (CEUs) and Professional Development Hours (PDHs) required for state and national licensing renewals. Please refer to the attached draft Statement of Objectives (SOO) for detailed requirements. Contractors who can provide these products/services are requested to identify if they are interested and submit, in writing, an affirmative response which includes as a minimum the following information: Company Information including: Company Name: Address: UEI/CAGE: Point of contact to include telephone number and email address for your company: Based on your professional experience in the private sector, would you consider this requirement to coincide with products/services provided in the commercial market? Specify your business type; large business, small business, small disadvantaged business, 8(a) certified small disadvantaged business, HUBZone small business, woman-owned small business, and service-disabled veteran-owned small business based upon NAICS 611430. Specify all that apply. Provide an additional NAICS code with justification that you would recommend as being more applicable. Does your company provide this product/service on a GSA Schedule, GSA IDIQ contract, or other Government-wide contract? If so, please provide the Contract/Schedule number and NAICS/special item number. If GSA is in the process of awarding a contract/schedule to you for this product/service, please provide the GSA point of contact name and phone number. Would your firm propose on this project as a prime contractor, prime contractor with subcontractor(s), prime contractor with team member subcontractor(s), or a joint venture? If you have proposed a joint venture, identify to the extent possible, your team members. Identify the business size of your team members or joint venture firms. If a teaming arrangement is planned, give details to the extent practicable on how the team will likely be composed. See FAR subpart 9.6 for Government policy on teaming arrangements and 8(a) Program regulations described in 13 CFR 124.513. Identify any projects completed in the past three (3) years for the same or similar scope. Include any Government contracts (Federal, State, or local) you have been awarded for this type of requirement. Also, include the contract number and a government point of contact. Identify if your company was the prime contractor or a subcontractor for these projects. Interested companies shall briefly explain how they would accomplish the objectives identified in the draft SOO, to include: Examples or screenshots of your administrative reporting dashboard. How does your system allow government administrators to track user progress, course completions, and assigned training hours in real-time? Describe the mechanism for controlling employee course access. How does your platform manage an online course approval process, and can approval hierarchies be customized? Detail your process for user account setup. How does your system capture and archive state license numbers and completion certificates? What is your data retention policy, and how can the government export this historical data? Provide a breakdown of your course library by discipline. Specifically, how many of your 2,000+ courses are focused on professional/technical engineering and architecture, versus general business or management topics? Courses must provide CEUs/PDHs that comply with state and national agencies. Describe your process for ensuring and validating that your courses are accepted by the various state licensing boards for engineering and architecture. Can you provide a list of state boards that have accepted your courses for credit? The requirement includes new course releases and updates. What is the average number of new engineering and architectural courses and live webinars you have added to your library annually over the past three years? Describe the security protocols and user authentication methods your platform uses to ensure that only authorized DAF personnel can access the training materials. Does your system have the capability to integrate with an organization's single sign-on (SSO) or identity provider? Describe your user support model. Beyond an initial webinar, what resources (e.g., help desk, knowledge base, technical support) are available to users who encounter issues with the platform or courses? Demonstrate your platform�s ability to meet Federal Information and Communication Technology (ICT) accessibility standards under 36 CFR 1194.1 (FAR Subpart 39.2). Vendors must provide a completed Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT) or an Accessibility Conformance Report (ACR) demonstrating how their web platform, self-paced courses, and live webinars support assistive technologies (such as screen readers, closed captioning, and keyboard-only navigation). Interested firms are encouraged to provide suggestions on products/services that can be included on this RFI to improve the development of this requirement. All responsible sources are encouraged to submit a capability statement in response to this notice. All questions and responses shall be submitted electronically to Mrs. Grace Pennington at grace.pennington@us.af.mil and Savanna Suggs at savanna.suggs@us.af.mil no later than Tues

description: 2026.09.24 - Solicitation Amendment 003 is issued to: 1. Extend the closing date of the Solicitation; 2. Respond to questions 4 through 10 received the during the solicitation period; 2026.09.18 - Solicitation Amendment 002 is issued to: 1. Respond to questions 2 through 3 received the during the solicitation period; and 2. Amend Section IV: Additional Information, in PART 3 - BID PREPARATION INSTRUCTIONS. 2026.09.16 - Solicitation Amendment 001 is issued to: 1. Extend the closing date of the Solicitation; 2. Respond to question 1 through 1 received the during the solicitation period; 3. Amend Article 1. Security Requirement, in PART 6 - RESULTING CONTRACT CLAUSES; and 4. Amend Annex C – Security Requirements Check List. This bid solicitation cancels and supersedes previous bid solicitation number 21470-31-5309193A dated May 11, 2026 that closed June 8, 2026 at 14:00 EDT. A debriefing or feedback session will be provided upon request to bidders/offerors/suppliers who bid on the previous solicitation. Urinalysis sample collection for offenders This requirement is for: The Correctional Service of Canada, Barrie, Ontario Trade agreement: This procurement is not subject to any trade agreement. Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers. Competitive Procurement Strategy: lowest priced compliant bid. Set-aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business: This procurement is not subject to any set-asides for Indigenous Suppliers. Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: This procurement is not subject to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement. Security Requirements: This contract includes security requirements. Nature of Requirements: The following is a summary of the statement of work for this requirement. The Correctional Service of Canada has a requirement to provide Urinalysis Collection Services for male offenders in Barrie and the surrounding geographical area. The work will involve the following: 1.1 Objectives: Consistent with the Mission Statement and Strategic Objectives of the Correctional Service of Canada (CSC), the contractor must provide a Urinalysis Collection Program for the Barrie area extending to the surrounding rural areas. 1.2 Tasks: 1.2.1 The Contractor must: 1. Upon referral, collect urine samples from federally released male offenders. 2. Provide a collector that must be of the same gender as the offender providing the sample. 3. Accurately label, store and package samples to prevent contamination or tampering. 4. Record necessary information, including time of collection, collector identification, and complete other required documentation. 5. Explain the urinalysis process clearly to offenders, maintaining a calm and respectful demeanor. 6. Handle potentially sensitive or uncomfortable situations with discretion and empathy. 7. Ensure the integrity of the sample by placing the required seals on the container, obtain signatures on the container, and prepare the container for shipment to the specified laboratory for testing. 8. Ship the samples with a bill of lading to the approved laboratory for testing. 9. Collect samples in compliance with Section 66(1) of the CCRA regulations, and CD 566/566-11. The contractor must provide protective gloves to the collectors. 10. Present the offender with form 1064-1 (Community Notification to Provide a Urine Sample) prior to the initial test or at the beginning of a new frequency of urine collection if CSC requests one, obtain the offender’s signature, complete the Chain of Custody Form 1065 for every sample collected and distribute copies of the form as directed. 11. Complete the urinalysis log sheets monthly, or provide a detailed invoice, or both, and forward them to the respective office responsible for the supervision of the offender. 12. Attend court hearings, meetings with auditors, or meet with CSC managers as requested. 13. For all cases assessed by CSC to meet the tandem supervision policy, the contractor must provide a collector and an additional member of its staff or a person approved by the project authority who must accompany the collector whenever a urine sample is collected in the offender's private residence or in an isolated community location (CD 715). CSC will brief both the collector and the additional member of the contractor's staff or approved person on safety concerns. 14. Immediately notify the CSC supervising parole office if the collector notes that an offender refuses or is unable to provide a sample, or displays any suspicious behaviour, or both. If this occurs outside the contractor’s established working schedule, the contractor must follow the National Monitoring Centre protocol. 1.2.2 Collection Schedule: 1. Normally, the contractor must perform collections during regular working hours, Monday to Friday, between 0700 hours and 1800 hours. 2. CSC may request that the contractor collect urine samples, from time to time, on weekends and after normal working hours. 3. CSC may request that the contractor collect urine samples on an emergency basis. The contractor must respond within 3 to 4 hours of being notified of an emergency requirement. 4. The contractor must respond within 24 hours’ notice for any non urgent requests to schedule collection. 1.2.3 Continuity of Services 1. The collector must provide 24 hours’ notice for cancellation of collections. The contractor must provide this notice to the Office Urinalysis Coordinator. 2. The contractor must provide a back-up for urinalysis collection, in case of illness, vacation, leave, or the inability to provide urinalysis collection services for at least 5 days. The contractor must obtain the Departmental Representative’s or Project Authority’s prior approval before the back-up performs any work. The back-up must also complete the CSC Urinalysis Collectors Orientation Program (at the contractor’s expense) before the back-up begins providing any urine collection services. 1.2.4 Support the Contractor CSC will: 1. Ensure that the contractor is provided with all necessary documentation including Regulations, Directives, and Guidelines for compliance to be maintained. 2. Provide procedural instructions for the surveillance, procurement and shipment of samples. 3. Refer offenders for urinalysis testing. 4. Establish procedures for shipment of samples to the CSC specified laboratory for testing. 5. Facilitate the process of securing Reliability Status security clearance for the contractor and/or subcontractor providing the services. 6. Provide the required paperwork, sample containers, courier bags, courier bills of lading, a cooler to store the collection samples and an appropriate security storage container for paperwork and referrals. 7. Provide a complete CSC Urinalysis Collectors Orientation Program prior to the collector commencing any urine collection services. The orientation includes safety procedures related to reporting negative offender behaviour to the CSC supervising parole office, and the National Monitoring Centre protocol. 1.2.5 Cancellations The contractor must not charge CSC when CSC provides at least 24 hours of notice of cancellation of collections. The Parole Officer Supervisor, CCC Manager, or Office Urinalysis Coordinator will provide this notice. When CSC provides less than 24 hours notice of cancellation of collection, the contractor may charge one-half the collection rate. The Parole Officer Supervisor, CCC Manager or Office Urinalysis Coordinator will provide the cancellation notice by Telephone notification or telephone message to the contractor. 1.2.6 No Show Fee If an offender does not show up for collection of a urine sample, the contractor may claim a maximum of 3 hours at the firm hourly rate. This fee shall only apply if the contractor scheduled a single collection. It will not apply when the contractor scheduled multiple collections for the same time period and at least one offender shows up. 1.3 Location of work: The Contractor must perf

title: RFSO -Coastal imaging, habitat classification, shoreline assessment in Canada
description: The Department of Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) has a requirement to establish a Standing Offer to provide professional services for the design, implementation, review, and maintenance of coastal imaging and habitat classification data and products for all Canadian coasts. The Contractor will use their expertise in coastal imaging, conducting aerial imaging and ground truthing surveys, and processing aerial imagery to produce open-source data products. The goal is to support DFO in shoreline classification, species, habitat and ecosystem vulnerability, and ocean protection. Specific goals include completing aerial imaging, stills, video, and ground truthing surveys, characterization and mapping of shoreline attributes, identification and characterization of biologically significant species and habitats, characterization of shoreline and nearshore species and habitats for wave exposure and oil residency indices, database creation and services, and publication of end products and reports. DFO will benefit from these services by efficiently collecting, processing, analyzing, and documenting data for the Ocean Protection Plan and spill response planning initiatives. Canada intend to establish one (1) Standing Offer (SO) to a qualified supplier who can provide the services to meet the general needs outlined in the Statement of Work Annex. The period of the Standing Offer will be from date of SO issuance until September 30, 2031. The Request for Standing Offers (RFSO) is to establish a National Individual Standing Offer for the requirement detailed in the RFSO, to the Identified Users across Canada, excluding locations within Yukon, Northwest Territories, Nunavut, Quebec, and Labrador that are subject to Comprehensive Land Claims Agreements (CLCAs). Any requirement for deliveries to locations within CLCAs areas within Yukon, Northwest Territories, Nunavut, Quebec, or Labrador will have to be treated as a separate procurement, outside of the resulting standing offers. The requirement is subject to World Trade Organization-Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-AGP), Canada - European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), and the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA).

title: APN_ONTARIO ARMOURIES SITE ENHANCEMENT PROGRAM VARIOUS ONTARIO LOCATIONS
description: Advance Procurement Notice CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR: ONTARIO ARMOURIES SITE ENHANCEMENT PROGRAM VARIOUS ONTARIO LOCATIONS (with Security Requirements) Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity in Hamilton and other locations in Southern and Central Ontario. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Description of the Project and Services This project will address infrastructure requirements to recapitalize Department of National Defence reserve and armoury infrastructure at multiple sites throughout Southern and Central Ontario. The delivery method for much of this project is anticipated to be Construction Management. The purpose of this project is to retain the services of a contractor to provide construction management services during the pre-construction and construction phases. The program is anticipated to include planned phased work packages implemented over a 7-10 year period while maintaining operations at the sites. Construction Management services are anticipated to support delivery of Track A (HMCS Star and CFRB Hamilton), are expected to support delivery of Track B (six armouries), and may be expanded in the future to include Track C (thirteen additional armouries). Major construction services are expected to include: Vertical infrastructure; construction of new facilities, recapitalization of existing facilities, and upgrades to building systems and components. Horizontal infrastructure; water distribution, wastewater collection, electrical distribution, communications systems, natural gas distribution, security infrastructure, site services, roads, parking areas and related civil works. The estimated construction cost is in the order of $100,000,000, consisting of approximately $60,000,000 for Track A and $40,000,000 for Track B. Additional future work associated with Track C may increase the overall program value by up to an additional $110,000,000. It is anticipated that this solicitation will be initiated in November 2026. This is conditional on receiving approval to proceed by the Department of National Defence (DND). Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS). Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, consultants or contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number (Project number on the MERX notice); Contract number 88064; and Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the consultants or contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a consultant or contractor: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation (Contract number listed on their request for sponsorship) being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package, and has submitted a proposal or a bid. DCC will  send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or bidder regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent or bidder will need to promptly cooperate with CSP  to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Lucia Apted Coordinator, Contract Services Defence Construction Canada TTcontracting@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent or bidder agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the bidder or proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.  Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

title: Subscription licenses to BNEF Bloomberg
description: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) supports informed decision-making on major industrial, economic development and clean technology initiatives. To fulfil this mandate, the Department requires reliable and up-to-date intelligence on global clean technology markets, investment flows, industrial trends, policy developments, emerging technologies and energy transition sectors. The Department has relied on BloombergNEF (BNEF) subscriptions to conduct research, monitor international market developments, assess investment opportunities, compare Canada's competitive position against other jurisdictions and support advice provided to senior government officials. BloombergNEF provides comprehensive market intelligence and analytical tools covering the clean technology and energy transition sectors that are not otherwise available through publicly accessible sources or other subscription services.

The scope of this project is to construct four (4) new accommodations buildings. The initial phase will consist of two (2) buildings with the potential of adding two (2) more buildings subject to approvals. Each building will each consist of a minimum 72 category II rooms in accordance with the DND Living Accommodations with a maximum of six (6) storeys. title: Independent Review of the Office of the DND/CAF Ombudsman
description: The Department of National Defence (DND) requires an independent third party to conduct a comprehensive review of the Office of the DND/Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) Ombudsman. The objective of this independent review is to examine the governance structure and authorities of the Office of the Ombudsman and benchmark the DND/CAF with the experience and practices of ombudsman functions from within the Government of Canada, other levels of government, and other similar democracies, including similar functions in allies’ militaries. This effort will help take forward Justice Fish’s Recommendation #103 to consider whether additional measures are needed to reinforce the Office of the Ombudsman’s independence and effectiveness.
